summary: Implemented the T039 per-pool extended-history research window artifacts: a per-pool window planner (per_pool_window.py) that supersedes T038's ten-million-block rule with a per-pool rule (coverage_from_block = pool_init_block, coverage_to_block = pinned finalized block), a finalized-pin agreement helper that rejects latest / non-finalized / wall-clock bounds, a sub-range splitter that respects the measured per-call log ceiling, an after-resume planner that emits pool_acquired_after_checkpoint_resume, a logical-call-count invariant that forbids per-block header fetches, a per-pool coverage report with per-pool data root, cost record, reconciliation verdict, and complete verdict (per_pool_coverage.py), and a per-pool operator runbook that names the historical-state endpoint able to serve the pinned depth (per_pool_window_runbook.py). 73 new tests cover: the per-pool rule itself (basic, two materially different pools over different-length windows, partial / full / no overlap, single-block window), the failed-resolution paths (pool_initialized_after_agreed_end, pool_initialize_resolution_failed), finalized-pin agreement (agreement, hash-casing normalise, number disagreement, hash disagreement, unavailability, non-finalized, malformed hash, no-latest-substitution), the plan validator (window-width mismatch, coverage-to-greater-than-pin, unknown outcome, unknown reason code, JSON-serialisability), checkpoint resume (boundary validation, suffix coverage, no-op at pin), idempotent re-runs (full prior coverage short-circuits, partial prior coverage does not), the logical-call-count invariant (valid / violation / resume), the per-pool coverage report (complete / incomplete / already_covered / failed_resolution, JSON / Markdown), data root / cost record / reconciliation validation, partition-owner reconciliation (clean + cross-pool attribution), the operator runbook (role routing, Markdown rendering, archive-state refusal, endpoints summary, JSON serialisation), failure-path reason-code coverage, pool-init-block-at-block-zero, and the budget ceiling (negative dimensions, explicit override). T038 modules / tests / dataset generations remain immutable historical evidence — no T038 file was edited. Full pytest run is 1340 passed / 6 pre-existing skipped; ruff format / ruff check / mypy --strict all pass on the new code and the wider tree.

residual_risks: The on-chain Initialize-scan resolver that produces the per-pool pool_init_block + pool_init_block_hash is an operator-side run-time action; the planner accepts operator-supplied Initialize evidence but does not perform the scan itself. The T039 contract requires the planner to consume resolved values and refuse to guess; the deterministic offline surface is fully covered by tests, but the live resolve-and-acquire loop still depends on T038's hook-scan resolver and the live endpoints.

The per-pool coverage report's already_covered outcome is the verbatim-reproduction case: a re-run over a window the durable checkpoint already qualified must produce no new chain reads. The planner records the range_already_covered_by_prior_run reason code and emits zero sub-ranges when the durable checkpoint fully covers the new pinned window; partial prior coverage does not short-circuit (the runner resumes from the suffix). This is exercised by tests but not yet wired into the runner.

The budget ceiling in the new module uses sensible defaults (1M logical calls, 1M HTTP requests, 8 GiB response bytes, 1M rows, 1B provider units, 24h elapsed time); the actual per-pool budget is operator-supplied in the live run. The contract requires that a declared budget halt the run rather than exceed silently; the cost record's exhausted_budget_dimension surfaces the dimension that hit the ceiling.

The historical_state_endpoint_alias in the runbook defaults to the secondary endpoint (alchemy_free) because that endpoint is measured to serve historical eth_call at the reference depth (ADR-010 / ADR-011). If the operator measures the primary endpoint to serve historical state for the configured pair, the runbook accepts an override; the builder refuses to construct a runbook when archive_state_capability_observed=False because that case is a documented failure path (endpoint_historical_state_unavailable).

No change to the existing T038 vocabulary. The T038 OUTCOME_POOL_INCLUDED and OUTCOME_POOL_INIT_OUTSIDE_WINDOW constants are unchanged; the T039 per-pool modules introduce a fresh outcome vocabulary (pool_acquired, pool_acquired_after_checkpoint_resume, pool_initialized_after_agreed_end, pool_initialize_resolution_failed) that does not cite the ten-million-block window. The T038 modules are untouched and remain the immutable historical evidence the contract requires.

PerPoolWindowPlan.__post_init__ allows coverage_from_block > coverage_to_block for failed-resolution outcomes (width == 0). PerPoolCoverageReport mirrors this so the audit trail can show the run halted before any chain read. The coverage_window_width property computes the inclusive span and returns 0 for failed cases.

The new modules' sha-pinned surface — PerPoolWindowInputs, PerPoolWindowPlan, PerPoolCoverageReport, PerPoolOperatorRunbook — does not perform any I/O, network, environment, or wall-clock read; every input is a pinned reference fact, an operator-supplied observation, or a planner output. The Markdown renderings and JSON serialisations are deterministic and the audit-trail records are reproducible.
